More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Private universities cannot be run for profit: Supreme Court orders disclosure of finances, fees et al.
items.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Central government, States and Union Territories (UTs) to collect detailed information about the finances, admissions, fees, use of surplus funds, staff recruitment and grievance-redressal systems of private universities and colleges. [Ayesha Jain v. Amity University, Noida and Others] In an order passed on 17 September, a Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and NV Anjaria issued the directions while making it clear that private universities could not be run as commercial ventures. “ No private university shall be allowed to be run as a profit-making institution. It has to serve a purpose with some sort of a cushion so that its finances/resources are responsibly managed to ensure smooth functioning of the institution and that the teaching and non-teaching employees are compensated suitably, ” the Court said. The Bench added that funds beyond this requirement could not be diverted towards purposes such as paying members of governing boards or providing facilities to them. items.title: EU sanctions cannot override contracts: Delhi HC orders SAP to restore software services to Nayara Energy
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday directed tech giant SAP India to immediately restore software and enterprise support services to Indo-Russian oil refining company Nayara Energy [Nayar Energy Limited v SAP India Private Limited & Anr] . Justice Vikas Mahajan said that SAP’s abrupt suspension of services following the European Union’s (EU) sanctions on Nayara in July 2025 was, prima facie, in breach of the contractual agreement between the two companies. The Court ruled that at the interlocutory stage, SAP “cannot take advantage of these unproven EU sanctions to argue that the performance of contract has become impossible”. “There is no doubt that the contractual relationship between the parties is strictly governed by the domestic laws of the Republic of India. The agreements gives a conscious and unambiguous primacy to the Indian laws in the event of any conflict with foreign rules or regulations,” the Court stated. items.title: Allahabad High Court acquits woman sentenced to death for killing her 3 children
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Tuesday acquitted a woman who was sentenced to death by a trial court last year in connection with the murder of her three minor children in June 2024 [Priyanka v State pf UP and Another] The accused Priyanka had been convicted along with her cousin-in-law Ashish alias Daini, who was sentenced to life imprisonment for conspiracy in the murder case. A Division Bench of Justice Siddhartha Varma and Justice Jai Krishna Upadhyay acquitted the accused of their charges after finding that the prosecution miserably failed to establish their guilt beyond reasonable doubt. "The conviction recorded by the learned trial court rests on statement of an uncorroborated, tutored, and contradictory child witness, coupled with a fatal failure to produce the best available evidence, unreliable deposition of PW-1 and investigative lapses. Therefore, the Court is inclined to grant benefit of doubt to the accused appellants on the ground of rule of caution," the Court said. items.title: Spoiling his own case: Bombay High Court pulls up Vijay Mallya for posting ED affidavit on X
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday orally reprimanded fugitive businessman Vijay Mallya for uploading an Enforcement Directorate (ED) affidavit onto X, noting that such postings undermine the efficacy of the court. [Vijay Vittal Mallya v. State Bank of India & Ors] Justice Milind Jadhav cautioned Mallya’s legal team that fighting legal battles on social media harms their own case. "Please make your client understand, this is not the way to do it. What happens is, it undermines the efficacy of the court then,” the judge remarked during the hearing. Justice Milind Jadhav The objection was raised by ED counsel, who informed the Bench that after emailing the affidavit to Mallya’s legal team at 4:30 PM, Mallya uploaded the entire document on X by 11 PM that same night accompanied by derogatory remarks. “This is not fair to Your Lordship's court...Your Lordship has not even had the chance to see it. The applicant should fight it out in court, not on Twitter,” the ED counsel submitted. The judge also added, “The problem is, he's spoiling his own case. If he's doing like this. items.title: Supreme Court refuses to entertain plea alleging misuse of SC/ST Act
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to entertain a plea challenging the 2018 amendment to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 which restored the bar on anticipatory bail and removed the requirement of a preliminary inquiry before registration of a first information report (FIR) under the Act. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana did not agree with the petitioner's contention that the Act was leading to reverse discrimination against people belonging to other castes. The Court observed that sufficient safeguards already exist under the law including the power of the courts to examine whether a prima facie case under the Act is made out or not. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The petitioner also questioned the payment of compensation to the victims under the SC/ST Act. The counsel representing the petitioner told the Court that ₹493 crore had been distributed as compensation to the victims and argued that the scheme was literally "inviting people to lodge FIRs". items.title: Supreme Court moots common platform to invest money deposited by litigants in courts
items.summary: The Supreme Court has proposed the creation of a common platform to pool and invest money deposited before different courts and tribunals by litigants [National Seeds Vs National Agro Seeds]. In a judgment delivered on September 17, a bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe observed that the present system lacks uniformity and can lead to financial loss for litigants Hence, the bench opined that deposits made before different courts and tribunals could be brought under a unified scheme and invested in financial instruments that are most beneficial to the parties. “ This common platform will not only create certainty in the interest rates and increase the ease of accessibility for litigants but will also ease the burden on Courts/Tribunals regarding how this money deposited is to be invested and dealt with ,” the Court said. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The Court made the observations while deciding a dispute between National Seeds Corporation Limited and National Agro Seed Corporation (India) concerning interest payable on money deposited during a challenge to an arbitral award. The Bench noted that there is presently no statutory prescription or uniform rule

items.title: Former MLA moves Madras High Court against TN government's decision to construct new Legislative Assembly building
items.summary: Former Mylapore MLA and DMK leader Dha Velu has moved the Madras High Court challenging the Tamil Nadu government's decision to construct a new Legislative Assembly and Secretariat complex at Foreshore Estate in Chennai's Pattinapakkam. Velu has sought quashing of a September 8 Government Order granting in-principle approval for the proposed complex. He has also urged the Court to grant an interim stay on further proceedings pursuant to the September 8 order, until the High Court decides the matter. The proposed complex is to come up on about 25.55 acres with a built-up area of nearly 20 lakh square feet. Chief Minister Vijay had announced the project in the Legislative Assembly on September 3 at an estimated cost of ₹1,200 crore, according to the petition. The government has since clarified that the Pattinapakkam site has not received final approval. Minister Aadhav Arjuna said on September 20 that only a Government Order had been issued so far and that a final decision would be taken by Chief Minister Vijay after a Detailed Project Report examines the feasibility of the proposal. items.summary: Nearly eight years after Mastercard Asia Pacific approached the Delhi High Court, a Division Bench on Tuesday began hearing afresh its challenge to a tax ruling which held that the Singapore-based company had a permanent establishment in India [Mastercard Asia Pacific Vs Union of India] While acknowledging the prolonged history of the case, a Bench of Justices Dinesh Mehta and Aditi Choudhary indicated that it would like to render a decision in the case. “ We were told on the last occasion that it was heard and then released, so let us decide, ” the Bench remarked. When Senior Advocate Harish Salve , appearing for Mastercard, referred to the arguments made by him previously, the Bench pointed out that it was considering the dispute for the first time. “ We just want to remind you that we are, for the first time, hearing this case, ” it said. Senior Advocate Harish Salve Since the petition was filed in 2018, it has been listed before various benches led by Justices S Ravindra Bhat, S Muralidhar, Vipin Sanghi, Manmohan, Rajiv Shakdher, Yashwant Varma, Prathiba M Singh, V Kameswar Rao and Dinesh Mehta . items.title: Kerala consumer court orders lift company to refund ₹2.69 lakh to retired High Court judge, wife
items.summary: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) at Ernakulam recently directed Nibav Lifts to refund ₹2.69 lakh with interest to a retired Kerala High Court judge and his wife after finding deficiency in services and unfair trade practice in connection with the proposed installation of a home elevator [Justice (Retd) TR Ramachandran Nair & anr v Nibav Lifts Private Ltd & anr]. A Bench of President DB Binu along with members V Ramachandran and Sreevidhia TN found that the company had failed to properly analyse whether the lift could be installed at the couple's residence before accepting the advance payment. The commission stressed that consumers cannot be expected to have the technical knowledge required to understand the consequences of installing such equipment and added that the responsibility was on the company, which had the necessary technical expertise to properly examine the site and explain the implications of the installation. items.title: Fountain Court's Alex Taylor on choosing a 47-year career in clerking over joining Fulham FC at age 16
items.summary: In July 1979, a 16-year-old Alex Taylor had a decision to make: take up a football apprenticeship at Fulham FC or join Fountain Court Chambers as a junior clerk, the lowest-paid and least familiar option on the table. He picked clerking. After 47 years, one senior clerkship and a chambers that grew from roughly 20 members to 116, Taylor is preparing to hand over the reins to Sian Huckett, who takes over as senior clerk in January 2027. In conversation with Bar & Bench's Pallavi Saluja , Taylor traces the evolution of clerking, from a paper-and-diary era with no formal career path to a sophisticated practice built on business development and client relationships. He also speaks on Fountain Court's deepening ties with India and a growing pipeline of Indian instructions into both London and Singapore. [Watch Interview] Edited excerpts follow. Pallavi Saluja (PS): Can you tell us how you got into clerking and the fact that you started at the age of 16? Alex Taylor (AT): It was through a careers officer at school. I was in a fortunate position, I'd been offered several jobs. Clerking was the least paid and the least familiar to my family. It really came down to a toss-up: take the clerk

items.summary: The Gujarat High Court on Monday adjourned journalist Ravi Nair's plea challenging his custody in a criminal defamation case in which he was convicted earlier this year for allegedly defaming the Adani Group. Nair had been released on bail during the pendency of his appeal against the conviction but was again taken into custody last week following the issuance of a non-bailable warrant against him by the Sessions Court. He has now moved the High Court to seek his release. Justice MK Thakker today granted Adani Enterprises more time to respond to Nair's plea seeking release from judicial custody. Senior counsel Mitesh Amin appearing for Adani submitted that he would like to put on record certain facts which may go against Nair. He thus sought a short date to file a response to Nair's plea. Advocate Abhik Chimni opposed the request, submitting that he was pressing for interim release of Nair. "They have no position to say anything in this matter. The Gujarat High Court which heard the case again on Monday, September 21, has now given two-day’s time for Adani Group to file a response to Ravi’s plea challenging the arrest. The case came up for hearing at the bench of justice MK Thakkar of Gujarat High Court. Though Ravi’s counsel pleaded for interim relief, the court postponed the case for two days. The counsel representing the Adani Group requested more time to submit legal and factual points in the case. Advocate Abhik Chimni appearing for Ravi asked why his client should spend even one day in jail in a case that was at an appellate stage. However, the court observed that the complainant should be given fair opportunity for responding to the notice. items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Tuesday pulled up the Punjab government for its failure to clear the defects in appeal filed by the State before the Supreme Court challenging the High Court's recent order for payment of pending Dearness Allowance (DA) to the State employees. Hence, it proceeded to summon the State's Chief Secretary over what it perceived to be a deliberate ploy by the State to avoid implementing the High Court's directions. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday deferred the hearing in the Public Interest Litigation (PIL) challenging the State government's decision to limit the singing of Vande Mataram to its first two stanzas at government functions [Girish Bharadwaj v State of Karnataka] . A Bench of Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice TP Vivekananda directed that the plea be listed after three weeks. This was after the State pointed out that a similar matter is pending before the Supreme Court. A petition filed by Carnatic vocalist TM Krishna is currently pending before the apex court challenging the constitutional validity of a 2026 amendment to the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, which makes intentionally preventing the singing of ‘Vande Mataram’ or disrupting an assembly engaged in its singing punishable with up to three years in jail. Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice T P Vivekananda The PIL before the High Court was filed by advocate Girish Bharadwaj through advocate Angad Kamath. It challenges the September 8 State government order providing that only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram be sung at State government programmes. items.title: Lakhimpur Kheri case: Supreme Court asks Allahabad High Court to examine allegations against trial judge
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday sought a report from the Allahabad High Court on allegations raised by Advocate Prashant Bhushan against the trial judge hearing the 2021 Lakhimpur Kheri violence case [Ashish Mishra Alias Monu v State of UP] . A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the Uttar Pradesh government to appoint a senior and experienced public prosecutor for the trial. "Let the State government take instructions and place on record its affidavit within two weeks as to which senior, experienced public prosecutor can be allotted for the case," directed the Court. Additionally, the Court asked Allahabad High Court Chief Justice Arun Bhansali to examine Bhushan's allegations against the trial judge. "Let a copy of this IA also be placed before the Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court to take note of, and let a report concerning the IA be submitted before us in a sealed cover before the next date."
